text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: usage-ingest-high-lag (PD#789012). Opened by pagerduty. Acknowledge/assign.

pagerduty: PagerDuty alert - service: usage-ingest-consumer. Severity: P1. Trigger: consumer lag > 1M messages for group 'usage-ingest-group' (topic: tokens-raw).

sarah (oncall): acked the pager. I'm on it.

mike (sre): looking at consumer lag now. which region/users impacted?

sarah (oncall): initial alert shows spikes in eu-west-1 and us-east-1. Affected pipeline: raw tokens -> token-aggregator -> metering. Potential customer impact: undercount for ingested tokens in last ~3h. Billing team pinged.

jason (billing): @sarah can you confirm which billing runs might include incorrect counts? We have nightly invoice generation at 04:00 UTC. If this persists we need a manual hold.

sarah (oncall): yes, nightly job for enterprise customers (commitment-based) at 04:00 UTC. ETA for a fix?

mike (sre): quick checks: consumer group lag table shows consumer offset stuck on partition 12/24. Running consumer-describe:
```
kafka-consumer-groups --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --describe --group usage-ingest-group
```
lag: ~1.2M on partition 12, others normal. consumer instance shows 'JOINING' since 3051234400.

ryan (infra): i'm checking the node hosting consumer-3. Looks like oom-kill event around 3051234300, pod restarted, but consumer didn't resume properly due to stale offsets in zookeeper.

mike (sre): can we force the consumer to rejoin? rolling restart of the consumer deployment might help. I'll try a graceful restart of consumer-3 only.

sarah (oncall): go for it. I'll update billing/cs.

mike (sre): performing restart...
```
kubectl rollout restart deployment/usage-ingest-consumer -n prod --selector=pod=consumer-3
# Or targeted pod: kubectl delete pod usage-ingest-consumer-3 -n prod
```

incident-bot: Deployment restart requested by mike.

mike (sre): restarted pod. consumer rejoined, but lag moved from 1.2M -> 900k in 2m. Streaming throughput low: 50 msgs/s.

ryan (infra): I see the node mounted a read-only disk for the local cache directory after the restart. Might be throttling. Remounting attempted.

mike (sre): remount fixed, throughput back to ~800 msgs/s. Lag now 200k and decreasing.

anya (cs): thanks. I'm drafting a note for the customers potentially impacted (enterprise invoices). Do we know if token counts will be lost or just delayed?

mike (sre): looks like delayed; messages are still in topic. No data loss reported. We'll run verification after backfill completes.

jason (billing): hold placed on nightly invoice generation for affected customers. Thanks. Please confirm when token counts are reconciled so we can unblock invoicing.

sarah (oncall): creating follow-up tasks: backfill verification + postmortem. Assigning owners.

sarah (oncall): action items: 1) Ensure consumer fully catches up (mike). 2) Run aggregation count diff for window 02:00-05:00 UTC to detect delta (jason + mike). 3) Notify customers and hold invoices if delta > 1% (anya + jason). 4) Root cause: node oom/restart -> investigate memory tuning (ryan + infra).

mike (sre): running quick SQL to compare raw token ingest vs metered tokens:
```sql
SELECT sum(tokens) as raw_tokens FROM raw_ingest WHERE ts >= '2026-03-14 02:00:00' AND ts < '2026-03-14 05:00:00';
SELECT sum(tokens) as metered_tokens FROM metering.aggregates WHERE ts >= '2026-03-14 02:00:00' AND ts < '2026-03-14 05:00:00';
```

mike (sre): initial numbers: raw_tokens = 18,452,310 ; metered_tokens = 17,950,120 -> delta ~2.8%. We'll run partition-level diffs.

jason (billing): delta > 1% so we keep invoices on hold. Also need to calculate per-customer deltas for top 20 accounts.

anya (cs): on it. I'll prepare a templated outreach explaining short delay due to ingestion backlog and that we're doing verification before invoicing.

sarah (oncall): we're going to run backfill job to reprocess the lagged partitions and re-aggregate. Estimated backfill time ~ 45 minutes at current throughput. Running now with higher parallelism.

mike (sre): starting backfill job:
```
./jobs/backfill --topic tokens-raw --partitions 12 --from-offset 123456789 --to-latest --parallelism 8
```

incident-bot: Backfill job started by mike. Job id: backfill-305123-01. Monitor at https://ci.prod/jobs/backfill-305123-01

mike (sre): progress: 25% processed (3051234700).

ryan (infra): increasing consumer autoscaler threshold to allow more pods during backfill.

mike (sre): progress 75% processed (3051234800). Lag now 12k.

mike (sre): backfill complete. Recomputed metering counts: metered_tokens = 18,451,980 (within 0.002% of raw).

jason (billing): verified top 20 accounts: deltas within noise threshold. Good to clear holds. Re-enabling nightly invoice job for affected cohort.

anya (cs): customer note sent to impacted enterprise customers. Template below: 
"We're running a short verification due to an ingestion backlog impacting token counts for a subset of accounts between 02:00-05:00 UTC. We've completed backfill and validated counts. No invoices were generated; the billing run will proceed with corrected data. Reach out if you have questions."

sarah (oncall): closing the pager. Root cause: node OOM killed consumer pod -> consumer didn't rejoin cleanly -> offset stall -> backlog. Follow-ups: set pod memory requests/limits, improve restart hooks to auto-reset offsets when necessary, add alert for consumer-join-state.

mike (sre): adding PR for memory tuning and a readiness probe that forces consumer rebalance after restart.

ryan (infra): will schedule infra runbook update and consider node memory pressure dashboard.

sarah (oncall): good job team. Postmortem owner: mike. I'll create the incident ticket and tag for 72-hour review. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Pager closed by sarah. PD#789012 -> Resolved.

mike (sre): putting summary in ops-postmortems and listing remediation PRs.

jason (billing): thanks all. No customer credits required.

anya (cs): closing loop with customers once postmortem is ready.

sarah (oncall): final note — keep an eye on autoscaler behavior during backfills, might need more graceful scaling.

[thread archived]
